principles: A hazard catalogue entry is not evidence of an implemented solver.
Each capability is qualified by hazard, regime, spatial and temporal envelope, output observable, and evidence class.
Synthetic invariants, analytical solutions, reference comparisons, held-out observations, operational skill, and presentation quality are independent evidence classes.
Missing data or unsupported physics must report unavailable rather than zero effect.

hazards.notes: Separate source rupture, ground motion, liquefaction and induced landslide claims.

hazards.candidate_reference: GeoClaw and published tsunami benchmark cases
hazards.notes: Keep earthquake, landslide, volcanic and asteroid source terms distinct.
Ash dispersion does not qualify lava, pyroclastic density current, lahar or eruption-source prediction.
Keep triggering probability separate from runout and exposure estimates.

hazards.candidate_reference: Published avalanche test cases and regional observational archives
hazards.notes: Terrain, snowpack, weather and human-triggering assumptions require separate provenance.

hazards.candidate_reference: LISFLOOD-FP; HEC-RAS-compatible benchmarks; existing Symtropy hydrology issues
Published coastal hydrodynamics benchmarks; specialist coastal model selected per equations
Regional soil-water, hydrology, crop and drought-indicator datasets
hazards.notes: A drought index is a diagnostic, not a complete causal model of hydrology, demand, crops or ecosystems.

hazards.candidate_reference: NOAA operational forecast archives and named forecast-verification suites
hazards.notes: Pin the forecast cycle and distinguish hindcast, analysis and operational forecast.

hazards.candidate_reference: Regional radar/reanalysis/observational verification datasets and published case studies
hazards.notes: These are related but distinct processes; no shared score substitutes for phenomenon-specific verification.

hazards.candidate_reference: WRF-Fire and identified fire-spread/smoke models under matched assumptions
hazards.notes: Surface fire, crown fire, fire-atmosphere feedback and smoke transport are separate capabilities.

hazards.candidate_reference: Meteorological reanalysis and forecast verification datasets
hazards.notes: Forecasting and downstream impacts on health, energy and infrastructure are separate claims.

hazards.candidate_reference: NASA Ames ATAP/PAIR; selected high-fidelity model outputs; GeoClaw for matched tsunami cases
NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center models and event observations
hazards.notes: Do not equate space-weather indices directly with local infrastructure damage without a qualified system model.

hazards.candidate_reference: Established compartmental/agent-based models and held-out surveillance data
hazards.notes: Separate transmission model, observations, intervention assumptions, privacy rules and operational decisions.

hazards.candidate_reference: Domain-specific ecosystem, crop/forest and remote-sensing observations
hazards.notes: Different biological processes need different equations and evidence; this entry does not assert support.

hazards.candidate_reference: NOAA SWPC observation/model products plus qualified grid/telecommunications models
hazards.notes: Correlated outages alone do not establish causal attribution.
